description.text: Our mission is to empower communities and make their knowledge accessible to everyone. We built Reddit with the belief that communities unlock the power of human creativity and create a sense of belonging and empowerment for their members. Our over 100,000 active communities have channeled the power of human creativity to grow Reddit since our founding. We believe the world needs community more than ever, and that this represents our greatest opportunity to further enrich the lives of everyone in the world. Overview: The Power of Reddit’s Communities Reddit is a global, digital city where anyone in the world can join a community to learn from one another, engage in authentic conversations, explore passions, research new hobbies, exchange goods and services, create new communities and experiences, share a few laughs, and find belonging. People are diverse and have multiple interests. Just like in a city, where citizens are part of multiple sub-communities, on Reddit, users often belong to multiple communities. At Reddit, users can dive into anything, and if a community does not already exist around a particular topic, they can create one. In the three months ended December 31, 2025, an average of 121.4 million daily active uniques (“DAUq”) around the world came together on Reddit – continuously adding to our longstanding and constantly evolving human archive of information.

about.description_short: Reddit is a community of communities. Built on shared interests and passions, it is home to the most open and authentic conversations online. Every day, millions of people post, vote, comment, and search for answers across nearly every topic imaginable, and brands build trusted relationships with their audiences. With 26+ billion posts and comments and more than 130 million daily active uniques, Reddit is one of the internet's largest sources of information. Learn more at www.redditinc.com . The Reddit app is available on the App Store and Google Play.

employees.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we had 2,555 employees, including 1,981 in the United States.

analysis_md:
# RDDT — Reddit, Inc.
Sweep run, 2026-10-13 (engine v5 re-run; supersedes the 2026-10-12 v4 pass — same conclusion, price moved $155.66 → $159.93). In scope: market cap ~$32.3B < $40B. Price $159.93 (Nasdaq quote API).

## What it is
The community platform: 100,000+ interest-based communities (subreddits) with volunteer moderation and user-generated content, 130.3M daily active uniques and 514.6M weekly active uniques in Q2 2026. Revenue is ~95% advertising ($762M of $805M in Q2 2026, +64% YoY); the rest is "other" — data licensing of its human-conversation corpus to AI labs (Google deal signed 2024 at a reported ~$60M/yr; OpenAI at a reported similar scale) plus premium. Asset-light: 91.3% gross margin in Q2 2026, capex ~0.2% of revenue. Public only since the March 2024 IPO ($34), so EDGAR history is 4 fiscal years (2022–2025) and OE-positive in exactly one of them — the entire analysis turns on whether the FY2025/TTM inflection is the new base. It is: Q1 2026 revenue +69% YoY, Q2 +61% (the 8th straight quarter above 60%), net income $253M in Q2 alone, TTM operating cash flow over $1B. Q3 2026 guided to $860–870M revenue (~+47–49% YoY) and $385–395M adjusted EBITDA.

## Owner's earnings (SEC EDGAR, filing-direct)
History (conservative OE = OCF − capex − SBC):
- FY2022: revenue $667M, OE −$155.6M (−$2.72/sh) — pre-profit
- FY2023: revenue $804M, OE −$132.4M (−$2.24/sh)
- FY2024: revenue $1,300M, OE −$585.8M (−$4.03/sh) — the IPO year: SBC spiked to $801.6M, of which **$534.7M was a one-time double-trigger RSU charge recognized when the IPO satisfied the performance condition** (FY2024 10-K)
- FY2025: revenue $2,203M (+69.4%), OE **+$341.0M = $1.69/sh** (OCF $690.9M − capex $6.7M − SBC $343.2M)
- Maintenance version FY2025 (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): only +$113.1M — far below the conservative figure because ΔNWC was +$425.8M (receivables build on +69% revenue growth; accounts receivable grew $241M in FY2025). That is growth working capital, not a quality red flag, but it is the honest pessimistic bound and a reason not to run the verdict off the rosiest base.
- The engine's normalized base (3-yr median OE/share) is **−$2.24/share → the preliminary v5 run returned Tier F on it**. That median is rejected, with cause: two of its three years are pre-profitability and the third is the IPO-SBC spike year. The TTM base below is filing-derived, covers four consecutive profitable quarters, and is the same treatment the APP pilot got.
- Balance sheet: no debt (engine net debt is null — no debt tags exist); cash & equivalents $953.6M at FY2025-end and ~$2.8B of cash + marketable securities at Q2 2026 (~$13.5/share). A $1B share repurchase program was announced with the FY2025 results (Feb 2026); $235M of buybacks executed in Q2 2026 alone.

**Base used: TTM owner's earnings through Q2 2026, from `ttm.py` (inputs quoted verbatim — no hand arithmetic):**
- OCF: FY2025 $690,875,000 (2025-01-01–2025-12-31) − prior YTD $238,909,000 (2025-01-01–2025-06-30) + current YTD $574,129,000 (2026-01-01–2026-06-30) = **TTM $1,026,095,000**
- Capex: FY $6,706,000 − prior YTD $1,484,000 + current YTD $2,224,000 = **TTM $7,446,000**
- SBC: FY $343,180,000 − prior YTD $174,484,000 + current YTD $169,288,000 = **TTM $337,984,000** (12.2% of TTM revenue, down from 15.6% in FY2025 and ~62% in the IPO year — but still 33% of TTM OCF; the deduction stays in full in every scenario)
- Diluted shares (TTM basis = current YTD weighted average): **202,326,864** (FY2025: 202,107,978)
- **TTM OE = $680,665,000 = $3.364/share** — passed via `--base-oe-ps`. ttm.py exited cleanly, no warnings.

## MOAT — score 6/10 (moderate-strong, not wide)
FOR — (1) A genuinely unique corpus: two decades of authentic, organized human conversation across 100k+ self-moderated communities, now scarce enough that AI labs pay to license it; users append "reddit" to Google searches by name — demand pull few platforms have. (2) Community network effects with free labor: subreddits, norms, and volunteer moderators are expensive to replicate and the archive compounds. (3) Emerging pricing power: global ARPU +36% YoY in Q2 2026 (U.S. +51%) — monetization compounding far faster than users (DAUq +18%). (4) Structural economics: ~91% gross margin, near-zero capex, $1M+ revenue per employee. (5) International runway: machine translation into 30+ languages; intl revenue +84% YoY in Q2.
AGAINST — (1) **Distribution is rented, not owned:** 77.7M of 130.3M DAUq are logged-out, much arriving via Google search; Google AI Overviews increasingly answer without a click, U.S. logged-in DAUq growth is nearly flat, the stock fell ~21% after the Q2 2026 beat on exactly this concern, and Reddit is reportedly weighing blocking Google's crawler as the 2024 licensing deal comes up for renewal — its biggest traffic source and a licensing customer are the same counterparty. (2) No lock-in: users multi-home across TikTok/YouTube/Discord/X; switching costs for readers are zero. (3) Ad business subscale vs Meta/Google; intl ARPU $2.26 vs U.S. $11.85 — the convergence is a hope, not a print. (4) Data-licensing revenue concentrated in a few AI counterparties with uncertain renewals. (5) SBC load: $338M TTM, ~33% of OCF. (6) Dependence on volunteer moderators (the 2023 API protests showed the community can revolt).
CAP = clamp(2 + 1.3 × 6) = **9.8 years**: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over the CAP, 15-year projection.

## DCF — final v5 run (TTM base $3.364/share, moat 6, default probabilities 10/25/30/25/10, default offsets/multipliers)
Growth: the engine blend is 48.9% (rev CAGR 48.9%, latest rev YoY +69.4%; OE/share CAGR undefined off negative bases), adjusted −5pp for the (artifactual) share-count trend and capped to a **35% base start**.
**Sanity check against actual prints (mandatory):** every scenario start (23/30/35/40/47%) sits *below* the latest revenue prints (Q1'26 +69%, Q2'26 +61%), and the super-bull start (47%) sits right at the Q3'26 revenue guide (+47–49%). Written reasons, per the standing rule: (1) deceleration is guided and steep — 69% → 61% → 47–49% guide in three quarters; (2) the TTM base already capitalizes the inflection (OE/share +99% vs FY2025) — starting growth at print level on the stepped-up base double-counts it, the exact error the v4 audit caught on APP; (3) the starts are OE/share growth rates that must be *sustained* (2-yr hold, then 9.8-yr fade), and the recent prints are ARPU-led (ARPU +36% on DAU +18%) off a small base — ARPU cannot compound at that rate for a decade; (4) margin expansion toward the guided ~45% adjusted EBITDA margin is what keeps the bull paths honest despite revenue-rate starts below the prints.
Price: **$159.93** — 47.5× TTM owner's earnings, OE yield 2.1%.

| Scenario | Likelihood | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15% | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | 23% | 0.75 | Google referral traffic compresses; licensing stalls; ad downturn | $51.24 | 7.2% |
| Bear | 25% | 30% | 0.90 | Growth decays to the 20s; ARPU gains slow; SBC stays heavy | $83.29 | 9.9% |
| **Base** | **30%** | **35%** | **1.00** | Guided deceleration continues; margins grind up | **$114.64** | **12.2%** |
| Bull | 25% | 40% | 1.10 | International ARPU converges; ad stack matures; licensing scales | $155.79 | 14.8% |
| Super bull | 10% | 47% | 1.25 | Growth holds near guide for 2 yrs; ~50% EBITDA margins; licensing reprices up | $236.90 | 18.9% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $122.98 (−23.1% vs price), IV@12% $176.38, weighted IRR 12.7%**
- **Tier by numbers: C.** Diagnostics: OE yield 2.1%; terminal value 27.1% of IV@15% (healthy — this is not a terminal-value story; the near-term cash flows themselves are too small for the price); scenario spread 4.6×; months since FY end 9.4.

## FLAGS — every fragility flag in the final dcf_numbers.json resolved
- **STALE_FY** (FY2025 ended 9 months ago): resolved by construction — the base is the `ttm.py` TTM override quoted above, computed in code from 10-Q YTD OCF/capex/SBC, not estimated.
- **DILUTION** (share count +52.3%/yr): an IPO artifact, not a run rate. The engine's window spans the pre-IPO weighted count (57–59M) → IPO/preferred conversion (145.5M in 2024; ~73M shares from preferred conversion plus 18.6M newly issued) → 202.1M (2025) → 202.3M (H1 2026 YTD, **+0.8% YoY** on the weighted diluted count). The engine's −5pp share-count adjustment is therefore too harsh against current reality, but it is kept (conservative direction, method-consistent) and noted here as a headwind the forward numbers don't deserve. The real continuing cost is SBC (33% of TTM OCF), deducted in full; the $1B buyback ($235M executed in Q2 2026) offsets issuance if sustained.
- **BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT** (>60% revenue jump): no divestiture, big M&A, or restatement — acquisition cash in FY2024 was $17.1M. The jumps are organic post-IPO acceleration (FY2024 +61.7%, FY2025 +69.4%) from the rebuilt ad platform, machine translation, and search-referral growth. No basis break to straddle; the real caveat is that all CAGRs are measured over the acceleration window itself, which is why the capped 35% start (not the 48.9% blend) is used.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2024): net income −$484.3M vs OCF +$222.1M, a $706M gap vs D&A of only $15.6M. The one-off is the IPO: $801.6M of SBC (dominated by the $534.7M double-trigger RSU recognition at IPO effectiveness) is non-cash, so it crushes net income while OCF adds it back. OCF is real cash; the divergence is why FY2024 conservative OE (−$586M, SBC charged as a real cost at the spike level) is a trough artifact, not a run rate. SBC has since normalized to ~12% of revenue.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (super-bull IV 4.6× super-bear): real. A company 30 months public with one profitable fiscal year has a genuinely wide outcome range. Confidence is capped at medium because of it.
- Substantive, though the mechanical flag did not fire: **BASE_DIVERGENCE** — latest FY $1.69 vs 3-yr median −$2.24 vs TTM $3.36 (the flag's test needs a positive median, so it surfaced as the preliminary Tier F instead). The median is the distorted one — it averages two pre-profit years and the $802M IPO-SBC year. Rejected; TTM used. This is the single biggest judgment in the run and it is documented, not silent.
- Not fired, noted anyway: **net cash** — the engine could not compute net debt (no debt tags; Reddit has no debt), so BIG_NET_CASH never fired, but ~$2.8B cash + securities is ~$13.5/share of the $159.93 price. Crediting it on top of the OE DCF still leaves the stock below the 15% hurdle — it softens, not changes, the verdict. LOW_OE_YIELD also just missed firing (2.1% vs the 2% tripwire): this valuation rests on growth, full stop. History is thin (4 FYs) even though THIN_HISTORY (trips below 4) did not fire.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The business is better than the stock at this price. Eight straight quarters of 60%+ revenue growth, EBITDA margins heading to ~45%, SBC leverage improving every quarter, $2.8B net cash — and the DCF still says C, because 47.5× TTM owner's earnings pre-pays the base case and most of the bull case. Even the super-bull scenario alone returns only 18.9% from $159.93: at this price no defensible weighting reaches Tier A, and only a bull-weighted one reaches B.
- **Method range (both ends are engine runs actually executed, not vibes):** 3-yr median base → **F** (no positive normalized OE); FY2025-only base ($1.687/share) with identical scenarios → weighted IV@15% $61.67, weighted IRR 8.4%, **Tier D**; TTM base (final) → **Tier C, 12.7%**. Every defensible method lands below the 15% hurdle — the disagreement is only about how far below. The TTM base is the filing-derived, current one, so the verdict sits at C, the optimistic end of the defensible range. If you believe the −5pp dilution penalty and the 35% cap are both too harsh (both arguable, see FLAGS), the number moves toward B, not A.
- What would change the answer: a Google-referral shock is the bear trigger (watch logged-out traffic and U.S. DAUq); licensing renewals (Google/OpenAI) repricing materially up is the bull swing item; SBC % of revenue is the cleanest quality gauge — if it re-accelerates, the OE story breaks.
- Margin-of-safety math: the stock clears Andrew's 15% hurdle at the weighted IV of **~$123**; with a real margin of safety against the bear case (bear IV $83), a buyer wants **~$100 or below**. At $159.93 you are paid for the bull case (bull IV $156) and insured against nothing.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: C** (weighted IRR 12.7% on the TTM base; tier_final = tier_by_numbers, no override — the numbers tier already sits at the optimistic end of the defensible F→C range)
- Confidence: **Medium** (high on the TTM base — it is filing arithmetic from ttm.py; medium-low on any single growth path — 4.6× scenario spread and a 4-year public history cap it there, per the WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD rule)
- One-liner: Genuinely inflected, high-quality community platform, moat 6/10 — TTM owner's earnings of $3.36/share are real, but at $159.93 (47.5× TTM OE) the weighted IRR is 12.7% (IV@15% $123); it clears the 15% hurdle only below ~$123, and with a margin of safety below ~$100.

# RDDT — Second pass (2026-10-13)

Verdict: **NO MATERIAL FINDING** — score stands. Tier C, weighted IRR 13.0%, weighted IV@15% $123 (price at pass 1: $155.66). score.json not touched.

## Pass 1's load-bearing assumptions attacked
- Base OE: TTM (through Q2 2026) owner's earnings $3.364/share, built from 10-Q YTD OCF $1,026.1M − SBC $338.0M − capex $7.4M, rejecting the 3-yr median of −$2.24/sh as distorted by pre-profit years and the $801.6M IPO-year (FY2024) SBC spike.
- Growth: engine blend 48.9% capped to a 35% base start; scenarios 23/30/35/40/47%, probs 10/25/30/25/10, OE mults 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25.
- Moat 6/10 (CAP 9.8y). Fragility flags resolved as: STALE_FY → TTM base; DILUTION (+52.3%/yr) → IPO artifact; BASIS_BREAK → organic acceleration, no M&A/divestiture; NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE (2024) → IPO SBC; WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD (4.6×) → confidence capped at medium.

## What was checked

### (a) Segment / disaggregation growth masked by consolidated figures
Reddit reports essentially one business; the filing disaggregation is revenue type and geography, both already in pass 1, and neither reverses it:
- Advertising: $761.6M in Q2 2026, **+64% YoY** — *faster* than consolidated +61%. The core is not being flattered by a dying line; if anything consolidated growth slightly understates the core.
- Other revenue (data licensing + Premium): $43.3M, **+24% YoY**, shrinking from 7.0% to 5.4% of revenue. This is the slow line, but at ~5% of revenue its drag on the consolidated rate is ~2pp and pass 1 already treated licensing as concentrated/uncertain-renewal (Google/OpenAI), not as a growth engine. Contracted-but-unrecognized licensing revenue cited at $62.0M for rest of 2026 and $30.1M for 2027 — small vs. a ~$3.2B revenue run-rate, confirming licensing cannot move the DCF base or growth start materially in either direction.
- Geography: US $638.1M +56%, rest-of-world $166.8M +84% (20.7% of total) — exactly the international-ARPU runway pass 1 credited in the bull case. No hidden sunset segment, no discontinued/legacy line found.

Sources: Earnings Anatomy Q2 2026 breakdown of the filing; StockTitan 8-K / shareholder letter summary; Motley Fool Q2 2026 call transcript takeaways.

### (b) One-offs that recur / structural costs dressed as one-offs
- The FY2024 SBC spike ($801.6M) remains a genuine IPO-vesting one-off: SBC has since fallen to 13.3% of revenue in Q2 2026 ($106.8M SBC + related taxes, +12% YoY in dollars against +61% revenue) and TTM ~12.2% in pass 1. No recurrence.
- Low cash tax rate (~1.6% effective in Q2, NOLs / valuation allowance on deferred tax assets) is noted as a future normalization risk, but there is no filing or guidance quantifying a near-term cash-tax step-up, and owner's earnings here is OCF-based (cash taxes already in OCF). No quantified basis to lower the base — flagged as a watch item only, not a revision.

Source: Earnings Anatomy Q2 2026 (tax line / valuation allowance discussion); shareholder letter via StockTitan.

### (c) Events after the last filing pass 1 used (Q2 2026, reported 2026-07-30)
- No new earnings, guidance change, M&A, product sunset, or major customer win/loss since Q2. Q3 2026 earnings are expected 2026-10-29 — after this pass. The Q3 guide pass 1 used ($860–870M revenue, +47–49%; adj. EBITDA $385–395M, ~45% margin) is still the standing guide.
- Google/OpenAI licensing renegotiation and "choppy" search referrals were disclosed *on* the Q2 call (2026-07-30), i.e. before pass 1 (2026-10-12), and pass 1 already priced them into the moat (6, not higher) and the bear/super-bear scenarios. Third-party tracker claims in August 2026 of a sharp drop in Reddit's share of ChatGPT citations (Promptwatch, described by its own trackers as provisional) and Google's 2026-08-04 "no special preference" statement are citation-share data, not referral-traffic or revenue data, with no quantified revenue impact from the company — insufficient under the second-pass rules (no change without quantified evidence) to move growth starts that already sit *below* the latest prints for documented deceleration reasons.

Sources: Barchart earnings preview (next release 2026-10-29, Q3 estimates); Motley Fool / BigGo Q2 call transcripts (Huffman on licensing "not binary", search referrals "choppy"); TechTimes Q2 coverage (WSJ 2026-07-22 Google negotiation report); The HOTH / AEO content summaries of Promptwatch citation tracking.

### (d) SBC / dilution trajectory vs pass 1's share-count adjustment
Confirms pass 1, and confirms its conservatism:
- Fully diluted shares 207.0M at Q2 2026: **+0.2% YoY net, +0.3% sequentially**; +0.9–1.0% gross before buybacks.
- $234.6M / ~1.49M shares repurchased in Q2 at ~$157; $760.4M authorization remaining.
- Management *lowered* full-year SBC guidance to low-to-mid-teens % of revenue (from high-teens) and guides gross dilution to the low end of 1–3% before buybacks.
- Pass 1 kept the engine's −5pp share-count adjustment (driven by the pre-IPO → IPO share-count window) despite calling it too harsh. The new evidence says that adjustment is still too harsh, in the conservative direction — it is a reason the score might be understated, not a quantified basis on its own to re-run: pass 1 already disclosed this exact sensitivity and its method range (D on an FY2025-only base to C final, toward B only if both the cap and the dilution penalty are relaxed). No new filing changes the TTM base arithmetic.

Sources: Motley Fool Q2 2026 call transcript (CFO Vollero); StockTitan shareholder-letter summary.

### (e) Thin flag resolutions re-examined
- DILUTION and NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE resolutions hold up against the Q2 call/letter (see d).
- BASIS_BREAK: no divestiture, M&A, or restatement surfaced in any search; growth remains organic ad-platform acceleration.
- STALE_FY: still correctly handled by the TTM override; Q3 results (2026-10-29) will be the next filing that could move the base.

## Why the score stands
Every check either (i) confirms a pass-1 input (SBC ~13% and falling as % of revenue, net dilution ~0%, ads-led growth, international +84%), (ii) was already disclosed and priced into pass 1's moat/scenarios (Google referral risk, licensing concentration and renegotiation), or (iii) is unquantified tracker/commentary data with no filing-grade revenue impact. The one slow segment (licensing/other) is ~5% of revenue — too small to mask the core in either direction. No material finding, no engine re-run, no score.json change.
